'''Nigel Williams-Goss''' (born September 16, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. He spent two seasons with the [[University of Washington]] [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Huskies men's basketball team]] before deciding to transfer before the 2015–16 season.

==High school career==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG Nigel Williams-Goss at the rim.JPG|Williams-Goss at the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]|thumb|upright|left]]

Nigel Williams-Goss played high school basketball at [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]] and was the program's first 4-year player and helped lead the team to a 124-8 record, including winning the High School National Championship in 2010 and 2012.<ref name="McDonalds">{{cite web|title=Findlay Prep’s Nigel Williams-Goss named to McDonald’s All-American team|url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2013/feb/14/findlay-preps-nigel-williams-goss-named-mcdonalds-/|date=February 14, 2013}}</ref> He maintained a 4.0 GPA throughout his time in high school, while attending classes at Henderson International School.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss’ Strong Faith Paves Way To Success|url=http://archive.usab.com/mens/u19/13_mu19_features_williams-goss.html|date=June 17, 2013}}</ref>

MaxPreps named WIlliams-Goss an honorable mention sophomore All-American in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/_YxfCGxkEeCkhgAcxJSkrA/boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm|date=April 21, 2011}}</ref> After helping lead Findlay Prep to a High School National Championship, while averaging 15 points, 4.9 assists, and 4 rebounds per game, he was named a third-team junior All-American by MaxPreps in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/article.aspx?articleid=d1d546fd-5d58-4414-8321-71305642ae0b&page=3|date=April 16, 2012}}</ref>

As a senior, Williams-Goss averaged more than 18 points and 7 assists per game and was named to MaxPreps' first-team All-American team, after leading Findlay Prep 54 consecutive wins, including a 35-1 record and a trip to the semifinals of the National High School Invitational in the 2012-13 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=MaxPreps 2013 Boys Basketball All-American Team|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/bqRarSiJFkCjG8PM2lhOZA/maxpreps-2013-boys-basketball-all-american-team.htm|date=April 11, 2013}}</ref> He was also named to  [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|Parade Magazine's All-America team]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss makes Parade All-America team|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2013/05/22/nigel-williams-goss-makes-parada-all-america-team/|date=May 22, 2013}}</ref>

Williams-Goss was named as to the prestigious [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2013 McDonald's All-American Game]]<ref name="McDonalds"/> Against the best high school seniors in the nation, he scored 10 points along with 6 assists, 2 rebounds, 2 blocks, and a steal, while shooting 4-for-6 from the field and 2-for-2 from the free throw line. He also won the 3-point contest during the McDonald's All-American game festivities.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss shines at McDonald’s All-American game|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/huskymensbasketball/2013/04/03/nigel-williams-goss-shines-at-mcdonalds-all-american-game/|date=April 3, 2013}}</ref> Williams-Goss was also invited to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], where he led the West team to a 102–98 victory over the East, delivering the game-winning basket, in which he stole the ball and converted a three-point play after sinking a layup and heading to the foul line for an additional point. He finished with 17 points, 4 assists, 3 rebounds, and 1 steal on 5-for-6 from 2-point range, 1–1 from beyond the 3-point arc, and 4-of-5 from the free throw line in 20 minutes of play.<ref>{{cite web|title=California Supreme Alumni Nigel Williams-Goss Shines in 2013 Jordan Classic Making the Game Winning Shot, and Leading the West Roster with 17 Points|url=https://californiasupremebasketball.com/2013/04/14/california-supreme-alumni-nigel-williams-goss-shines-in-2013-jordan-classic-making-the-game-winning-shot-and-leading-the-west-roster-with-17-points/|date=April 14, 2013}}</ref>

===Recruiting===
{{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="He is a great floor general. He is very intelligent and has high, high basketball I.Q. He understands what it takes to win and is a great leader. Guys like him don't come around very often."|source=— [[Lorenzo Romar]], Washington Head Coach.<ref name="LOI">{{cite web|title=Romar Signs Another Guard To Next Year's Class |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=749597&SPID=126628&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=208025529 |date=November 16, 2012 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160514043914/http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=749597&SPID=126628&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=208025529 |archivedate=May 14, 2016 |df= }}</ref>}}

In December 2010, after beginning his sophomore year at Findlay Prep, Williams-Goss announced his commitment to UNLV. At the time he was being heavily pursued by the Rebels, along with Arizona, Washington, Oregon, and Oregon State, with increased interest from Georgetown and Connecticut.<ref>{{cite web|title=Findlay Prep sophomore guard Nigel Williams-Goss verbally commits to UNLV|url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2010/dec/15/williamsgoss-commit-121510/|date=December 15, 2010}}</ref> In April 2011, [[Lon Kruger]] jumped ship from the head coaching job at UNLV to become the new head coach at Oklahoma. Two weeks later, Williams-Goss decommitted from UNLV, giving other programs, including the Rebels' coaching staff a chance to court him.<ref>{{cite web|title=Findlay Prep sophomore Nigel Williams-Goss officially de-commits from UNLV|url=http://lasvegassun.com/news/2011/apr/17/findlay-prep-sophomore-nigel-williams-goss-officia/|date=April 17, 2011}}</ref>

Even though he re-opened his recruitment, William-Goss was still interested in attending UNLV and visited there many times, but after his junior year in high school, he planned visits to Harvard, Washington, Oklahoma or Missouri<ref>{{cite web|title=Updates from Findlay Prep on UNLV recruits Anthony Bennett, Nigel Williams-Goss and Chris Wood|url=http://vegasseven.com/2012/04/19/updates-findlay-prep-unlv-recruits-anthony-bennett-nigel-williams-goss-chris-wood/|date=April 19, 2012}}</ref> In May 2012, Williams-Goss pledged his commitment to Washington.<ref>{{cite web|title=Special player blog: Williams-Goss commits|url=https://recruitingspotlight.wordpress.com/2012/05/30/special-edition-player-blog-williams-goss-commits/|date=May 30, 2012}}</ref> He signed with the Huskies during the early signing period later that year.<ref name="LOI"/>

==International career==

Williams-Goss helped the USA win a gold medal in the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|2013 FIBA U19 World Championships]] in the Czech Republic, while averaging 7.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 0.8 steals, while shooting 49.1 percent from the field, 42.1 percent from beyond the 3-point line, and 90 percent from the free throw line.<ref>{{cite web|title=ELEVENTH FIBA MEN'S U19 WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP – 2013|url=http://www.usab.com/history/u19-mens/copy-of-eleventh-fiba-mens-u19-world-championship-2013.aspx|date=August 7, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==

===Freshman year===
As a freshman, Williams-Goss started every game, while averaging 13.4 points, 4.4 assists, 4.4 rebounds, and 1.1 steals. His stellar season earned him a selection to the All-[[2013–14 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]] Freshman Team.<ref>{{cite web|title=2013-14 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2014/03/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|date=March 10, 2014}}</ref> He led the Pac-12 conference freshmen in scoring, assists, and assist-to-turnover ratio (1.6). He set a new UW freshman single-season record with 140 assists. Despite his phenomenal year, UW finished with a disappointing 17-15 record (9-9 in Pac-12 games), losing in the first round of the Pac-12 Tournament to Utah, and missed the postseason for the first time since 2007, after declining an invitation to the CBI.<ref name="UW Profile">{{cite web|title=Washington Basketball Profile: Nigel Williams-Goss|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208952660|accessdate=April 16, 2015}}</ref>

In his first collegiate game, he posted 6 points, 6 assists, 3 rebounds, 3 steals, and a season-best 1 block on 2-for-7 field goal shooting and 2-for-2 from the free throw line in an 88-78 win over inner-city rival Seattle University.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Basketball Box Score - Seattle University vs Washington |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/pdf9/2562912.pdf |date=November 10, 2013 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601163328/http://www.gohuskies.com/pdf9/2562912.pdf |archivedate=June  1, 2016 |df= }}</ref> On November 17, he had 22 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, and a season-high 3 steals on 9-for-15 from the field and 4-for-5 from the charity stripe in a 92-80 win over Eastern Washington.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel-Williams BOSS: Freshman Leads UW Rally Over EWU|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209311234&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 17, 2013}}</ref> On November 26, he scored 20 points, along with 6 assists and 3 assists on 5-of-8 2-point shooting, 1-of-1 from 3-point, and 7-of-8 free throws in an 83-79 win over Montana.<ref>{{cite web|title=3-J Wilcox Rescues Huskies In 83-79 Rally Past Montana|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209324972&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 26, 2013}}</ref> On January 18, 2014, Williams-Goss posted 17 points, 7 rebounds, 6 assists, and 1 steal on 3-for-7 2-pointers, 3-for-5 from 3-point land, and 2-for-3 free throws in a 79-67 loss to Stanford.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stanford Hands Washington 79-67 Loss|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209378756&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=January 18, 2014}}</ref> On January 25, he set a new UW freshman single-game scoring record with 32 points in come-from-behind 87-81 win over Oregon State, in which he shot 7-for-11 from 2-point range, a season-best 3-for-4 from beyond the 3-point line, 9-for-10 from the free throw line, along with 5 87-81|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209386033&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=January 25, 2014}}</ref> On February 22, Williams-Goss dished out a season-high 10 assists to go along with 14 and 2 steals on 6-of-10 2-point field goals, 1-of-2 3-pointers, and 2-of-3 free throws om 30 minutes, in a 72-49 win over cross-state rival Washington State.<ref>{{cite web|title=Williams-Goss, Andrews Lead Huskies’ 72-49 Roll Over WSU|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209420741&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=February 28, 2014}}</ref>

===Sophomore year===
As a sophomore, he led the [[2014–15 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|2014–15 Huskies]] in points (15.6 scoring average) and assists (5.9 per game). He also contributed 4.7 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game, while starting in 30 of the team's 31 games.<ref name="UW Profile"/> His standout sophomore season earned him second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] in the [[2014–15 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball season|Pac-12]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2014-15 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://pac-12.com/article/2015/03/09/2014-15-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors|date=March 9, 2015}}</ref> He was also named as a third-team [[Academic All-American]], while boasting a 3.74 cumulative GPA in pre-social science.<ref>{{cite web|title=NWG Named Capitol One Third Team Academic All-American |url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=209909801 |date=February 26, 2015 |deadurl=yes |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601163330/http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30200&ATCLID=209909801 |archivedate=June  1, 2016 |df= }}</ref> Washington began the year with an 11-0 record, including impressive wins over Oklahoma and San Diego State, matching the best start in Lorenzo Romar's tenure as the Huskies' coach. Despite such a promising start, Washington would lose 15 of its last 20 games, finishing with a 16-15 record (5-13 in Pac-12 games), losing in the first round of the Pac-12 Tournament to Stanford, and missed the postseason yet again, after declining an invitation to the CBI.

In his first game as a sophomore at Washington on November 14, 2014, Williams-Goss grabbed a career-high 12 rebounds, along with 10 points, 7 assists, 2 steals, and 1 block on 5-of-5 2-point shooting in a 77-59 win over South Carolina State.<ref>{{cite web|title=Huskies Cruise Past SC State, 77-59|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209766842&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 14, 2014}}</ref> On November 28, he dished out a career-high 12 assists to go along with 21 points and 7 rebounds on 6-for-14 field goals and 5-for-6 free throws in an 80-70 win over Long Beach State.<ref>{{cite web|title=Williams-Goss' Double Double Lifts UW Past Long Beach State, 80-70|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209786152&DB_OEM_ID=30200|date=November 28, ===Junior year===
{{quote box|width=23em|align=right|quote="Nigel is a proven high-level player who possesses all of the qualities that we admire here at Gonzaga. He’s a very driven, team-oriented guy and is excited to be a part of this program. He’s also been great in the classroom as an Academic All-American, which fits in with our history of academic success. We are really excited to get him in here and help him develop the next part of his game."|source=— [[Mark Few]], Gonzaga Head Coach.<ref name="GU transfer">{{cite web|title=Gonzaga Men's Basketball Adds UW Transfer Nigel Williams-Goss|url=http://www.gozags.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050615aaa.html|date=May 6, 2015}}</ref>}}

In April 2015, Williams-Goss announced he was leaving Washington and transferring to another school. Even though he had a great relationship with Coach Romar and his teammates, he was uncomfortable with the changes surrounding the program and the team's consistent losing.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss explains why he’s leaving Washington|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/uw-husky-basketball/nigel-williams-goss-explains-why-hes-leaving-washington/|date=April 10, 2015}}</ref>

He initially claimed he was considering UNLV, Texas, Georgetown, Michigan State, Arkansas, and Gonzaga.<ref>{{cite web|title=Washington transfer Nigel Williams-Goss told @CBSSports he is considering UNLV, Texas, Georgetown, Michigan State, Arkansas, and Gonzaga|url=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/586628584040706048|date=April 10, 2015}}</ref> A couple days later, he said he would take visits to UNLV, Providence, Texas, and Georgetown, with Michigan State also in the mix.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss told @CBSSports he will visit UNLV this wknd, Providence (4/25), Texas (5/1), + Georgetown (5/8). Mich St also in mix |url=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/588024600769990656|date=April 14, 2015}}</ref> After visiting UNLV and Providence, Williams-Goss cut his list to 4 (UNLV, Providence, Gonzaga, and Ohio State), with plans to visit Gonzaga and Ohio State.<ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss told @CBSSports he will visit Ohio State on 5/8. Visits Gonzaga this weekend. Also considering PC + UNLV. List cut to 4 |url=https://twitter.com/JonRothstein/status/592858097317781504|date=April 27, 2015}}</ref> He called off his trip to Ohio State after committing to Gonzaga during his recruiting trip. He would have to redshirt the 2015–16 season before having two years of eligibility to play at the beginning of the 2016–17 season.<ref name="GU transfer"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Nigel Williams-Goss will transfer to Gonzaga|url=http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2015/may/03/nigel-williams-goss-will-transfer-gonzaga/|date=May 3, 2015}}</ref> Williams-Goss cited the Zags' track record of developing players during their redshirt year, winning at a high level, and their up-tempo offense which includes a ton of ball screens for his commitment to Gonzaga.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gonzaga Basketball: Introducing our newest Zag, repping #5 Nigel Williams-Goss! Welcome to the squad Nigel!|url=https://twitter.com/ZagMBB/status/596069451914715138|date=May 6, 2015}}</ref>

Throughout his junior season, Williams-Goss provided his best season in college with his only season in Gonzaga. In 38 games he played with for Gonzaga, he recorded the most points off of his best overall shooting percentage, rebounds, and steals per game while also playing the least amount of minutes per game throughout his college career. In addition to those results, he was also named the [[West Coast Conference]]'s Newcomer of The Year and the [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|West Coast Conference's Player of The Year]], as well as became a member of the All-West Coast Conference First Team, a member of the [[Academic All-American]] First Team, and was a consensus All-American Second Team for the help he provided for the 37–2 Gonzaga Bulldogs. Not only that, but he also helped lead Gonzaga to its first ever NCAA Championship match, where they ultimately lost to the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. After the end of the NCAA Tournament, Williams-Goss was one of a record-high 182 underclassmen to declare for the [[2017 NBA Draft]], with him signing up with an agent on the day of his declaration.
